newsitem.title: USA: CBOT nearby soy products end lower on crush data.
newsitem.headline: CBOT nearby soy products end lower on crush data.

text.p: A strong weekly crushing pace caused nearby soymeal and soyoil futures to settle with modest to moderate losses on the close Friday, traders and analysts said.
Thursday, National Oilseed Processors Association reported a stronger-than-expected weekly crush of 25.632 million bushels.
That figure exceeded trade expectations for 24.00 to 25.45 million bushels and implied growing supplies of soyoil and soymeal, traders said.
Trade in both pits was described as lackluster.
The higher crush also pressured cash soymeal values. Some dealers in Illinois and Indiana quoted basis offers $2.00 to $6.00 per ton lower Friday.
Competition from less expensive vegetable oils has kept pressure on soyoil prices in export markets, cash traders said.
July soymeal ended $2.60 lower at $273.60 per ton, with other months $1.20 lower to $2.00 higher. July soyoil closed off 0.01 cent at 23.46 cents a lb, with the rest steady to 0.07 higher.

"The Malaysians have been very aggressive sellers of palm olein lately," said one soyoil trader. "They're moving the product because they're looking at extremely large northern hemisphere oilseed crops."
On the day in soymeal trade, ADM sold 300 lots July and bought 300 August and 200 July. Cargill bought 200 lots July,pit traders said.
In soyoil trade, ADM bought 300 lots July and Cargill sold 300 July and 100 August, traders said.
Soymeal futures volume was estimated by CBOT at 23,000 lots, compared with Thursday's actual volume of 32,361 lots. Soyoil volume was pegged at 17,500 lots, against Thursday's 20,779 lots.
